headline: A plague lab death in Siberia. Russia says pneumonia.
summary: A technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, about 3,000 miles east of Moscow, fell ill and died. Russia's health agency says pneumonia of unknown cause and no plague bacteria in her samples. A local outlet says she broke a test tube. 189 contacts are in hospital. Rubio calls it "cause for focus."
cover_answer: No. One woman died in Siberia. Nobody else is sick.
table_question: Someone says "nothing to see here." When do you believe them?

5-7.script: A scientist in Russia who studied germs got very sick and died. She worked in a lab so far away a plane would take all day to get there. Doctors are checking everyone she was near, and so far nobody else is sick. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Plague is a scary word. The script never says it, and the plane ride puts the lab far away.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old takes one vivid feature, and Cantor says a named disease that can reach them is what frightens at this age. So the script drops the word plague, puts the lab a day's flight away and ends on the checking. Expect "can I catch it?" No. Nobody else is sick, and it is a world away.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: A lab worker in Siberia who studied plague got sick and died. Russia says pneumonia, cause unknown. A local reporter says she broke a test tube. Doctors put 189 people she met in hospital to watch them, a smoke alarm before any fire. Nobody else is sick.
8-12.why: A chain they can follow, and a smoke alarm for the quarantine.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether adults tell the truth, so the script runs the chain: a lab, a death, two accounts, 189 people watched. The smoke alarm says why a quarantine is not a sign anyone else is ill. Expect "so which story is true?" Nobody outside Russia knows yet.

13-17.script: Why does the US care about one death in Siberia? A plague-lab technician died, Russia says pneumonia, a local outlet says a broken test tube, and 189 contacts are in hospital. Second: Russia deleted its own warnings. Does that make it more likely, or just less known?
13-17.why: The official account, and the deleted posts.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: Russia's account, a death from pneumonia, and the posts deleted after it. The script hands them both and asks what deletion proves: less than it feels. Expect "is this how COVID started?" Nobody knows. Plague is treatable with antibiotics when caught early.

5-7.a: No. One woman died, very far away. The doctors checked everyone near her and nobody else is sick.

8-12.a: A germ that gets into the lungs. It is serious, and antibiotics treat it if doctors catch it early.

8-12.q: Why are 189 people in hospital if nobody is sick?
8-12.a: To watch them. If one gets sick, the doctors are already there. So far none has.

13-17.q: Why does the US care about one death in Siberia?
13-17.a: Plague spreads, and Russia's accounts differ. Rubio calls it cause for focus.
A state channel pulled five articles. A town warning vanished. What it means is open.
